newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Mt Leyshon first qtr profit. [Corrected 7:12 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Mt Leyshon first qtr profit. [Corrected 7:12 gmt]

text.p: Mt Leyshon Gold Mines Ltd on Wednesday reported a 1996/97 first quarter profit after tax of A$16,000, down on the June quarter result of A$465,000.

In its quarterly report, Mt Leyshon said gold production of 37,123 ounces was 4.9 percent lower than in the June quarter, reflecting a lower average head grade and the cessation of heap leach production.
"Overall mine operating cost increased to A$474 per ounce and the company recorded a break even result," executive chairman Tony Palmer later told the company's annual meeting.
However, Palmer later told shareholders that 1996/97 held promise for a return to production and profit levels in keeping with a mine of the quality of Mt Leyshon.

With just under five years of mine life remaining at the current production rate, exploration success was essential for the continuation of operations in the Charters Towers region in Queensland and the company had committed A$2.7 million to exploration this year, he said.

Palmer said Jindivik and S1 prospects had been assigned a priority one ranking and along with other targets defined in the 1995/96 field programme would be the subject of detailed follow up in the year ahead.

He told shareholders that in the past three months the company had had to mobilise additional earth moving equipment to unload the mine's eastern pit wall which was showing signs of instability, which would cost A$7 to 9 million.
As a result, the company had in place an overdraft facility to meet ongoing working capital requirements which was expected to be extinguished before the end of the financial year.

Palmer said that on a positive note the scats project, which would add an estimated 8,000 ounces to annual gold production, was completed two weeks ahead of schedule and 17 percent below budget at a cost of A$1.9 million.
The project will treat the large quantity of scats - some 1.3 million tonnes a year - which are generated when ore is ground and which would otherwise be rejected as waste, he said.
The Mt Leyshon mine reserve stood at 1.17 million ounces of gold at end-March, he said.
